question: What is the primary goal of emergency triage?

options.A: Sorting patients by severity of illness

explanation: Triage organizes patient flow so that life-threatening cases receive care first. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h1)

question: In an emergency ward, why might a quiet, silent patient need attention before someone who is shouting in pain?

options.A: Quiet patients pay higher insurance fees
options.B: Quiet patients might have silent, deadly conditions
options.C: Loud patients are always faking their symptoms
options.D: Hospital rules demand silence in the waiting room

explanation: You've got this! Quietness can mean a patient is slipping into unconsciousness or severe shock, which is much more dangerous than localized pain causing someone to shout. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h1)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the emergency survey?
explanation: The B step evaluates respiratory rate, effort, and oxygenation after the airway is secured. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h2)

question: When checking an emergency patient using ABCDE, when is it safe to move from Airway to Breathing?

options.A: Only after the airway is confirmed clear and secure
options.B: Whenever the nurse finishes checking the pulse
options.C: As soon as the patient opens their eyes
options.D: After the doctor arrives at the bedside

explanation: Think of it like building a house—you must finish one step before the next. The ABCDE sequence is strictly linear, so you stabilize the airway before moving to breathing! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h2)

question: Which airway maneuver is safest to use for a trauma patient who might have a neck injury?
explanation: Great choice! The jaw-thrust opens the airway without moving or bending the neck, protecting the cervical spine from further harm. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: An unconscious patient still has a gag reflex and needs an airway device. Which one is best to use?
explanation: An oropharyngeal airway can trigger vomiting if the gag reflex is active, but a nasopharyngeal airway is much better tolerated by the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is a major warning sign that a patient has developed a tension pneumothorax?

options.A: Equal breath sounds in both lung fields
options.B: Flushing and redness of the face
options.C: Tracheal deviation away from the affected side

explanation: As pressure builds up inside the chest, it pushes the windpipe (trachea) and vital organs toward the healthy, unaffected side. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: Why does a tension pneumothorax cause a sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure?

options.A: The patient stops breathing completely within seconds
options.B: Trapped air compresses the heart and great vessels
options.C: Infection destroys the walls of the blood vessels
options.D: Blood rushes rapidly into the abdominal cavity

explanation: Imagine air building up and squeezing the heart like a tight fist—this pressure prevents blood from flowing back to the heart, causing blood pressure to crash. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the most common cause of shock in trauma patients?
explanation: Hemorrhage rapidly depletes circulating blood volume, leading directly to hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h5)

question: Why can relying only on a normal blood pressure reading be dangerous in the early stages of shock?

options.A: Systolic pressure always rises before it drops
options.B: Blood pressure cuffs are rarely accurate in emergencies
options.C: Compensatory mechanisms maintain pressure despite blood loss
options.D: Pain medications artificially stabilize blood pressure

explanation: The body fights hard! The heart beats faster and blood vessels squeeze tight to keep the blood pressure looking normal, even when the patient has already lost a lot of blood. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h5)

question: What are the three components of the Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Airway status, breathing depth, pulse rate
options.B: Reflex speed, muscle tone, grip strength
options.D: Eye opening, verbal response, motor response

explanation: The GCS assesses these three specific neurological indicators to grade a patient's level of consciousness. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h6)

question: A confused trauma patient smells of alcohol. What vital checks must the nurse do first?

options.A: Family members for signs of substance abuse
options.B: Blood glucose level and oxygen saturation
options.C: Previous psychiatric history in the folder
options.D: Exact time of their last alcoholic drink

explanation: Never assume it's just alcohol! Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) or low oxygen (hypoxia) can mimic drunkenness and cause serious brain damage if missed. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h6)

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the SAMPLE history mnemonic?
explanation: In the SAMPLE history, A stands for allergies to medications, food, or environmental triggers. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why is keeping an emergency trauma patient warm such a big priority?

options.A: Warmth prevents the patient from falling asleep
options.B: Hypothermia increases the risk of local skin infections
options.C: Patients complain loudly about cold air-conditioning
options.D: Cold temperatures worsen bleeding by impairing blood clotting

explanation: You're doing great! Being cold stops the blood from clotting properly. Combined with acid buildup and blood loss, it creates a very dangerous situation for trauma patients. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h7)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical handover?
explanation: SBAR provides a standardized framework for concise and effective interprofessional communication. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h8)

question: Why is writing down patient care notes immediately (contemporaneous documentation) so important in emergency nursing?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers
options.B: It allows relatives to read the notes in real time
options.C: It satisfies hospital accountants for billing purposes
options.D: It prevents errors caused by forgetting details later

explanation: In a busy emergency unit, things happen fast. Writing down care as it happens ensures you don't forget crucial details when your mind is pulled to the next crisis. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h8)
